You are a research scientist doing open-ended, data-driven research on the dataset(s) described below. State exactly ONE original, falsifiable hypothesis about relationships in these dataset(s) that could be verified with a robust statistical test.

##### DATASET DESCRIPTION #####

### DATASETS: ###

Dataset Name: nls_raw.csv
Dataset Description: Respondent-year panel of survey responses on schooling, work, and family outcomes.

### COLUMNS: ###

id:
  Anonymized respondent identifier.

year:
  Survey year of the observation.

age:
  Respondent age in years at the survey year.

sex:
  Respondent sex (categorical: female, male).

race:
  Self-reported race/ethnicity category.

years_of_schooling:
  Highest years of completed schooling.

employed:
  Employment status in the survey year (binary: 0, 1).

annual_income:
  Reported annual income in nominal US dollars.

urban_residence:
  Whether the respondent lived in an urban area (binary: 0, 1).

num_children:
  Number of children in the household.

Guidelines:
1. Use ONLY the provided dataset(s); do not invent columns or synthetic data. You may derive composite variables from existing columns.
2. Pick an interesting context (e.g. a subset defined by categorical values), interesting variables, and an interesting relationship between them.
3. The hypothesis must be verifiable with a robust statistical test.
4. Make it specific and self-contained: name the outcome variable(s), the explanatory variable(s), and the expected direction of the relationship.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else:
{"hypothesis": "<your one-sentence falsifiable hypothesis>"}

##### DATASET DESCRIPTION #####
TCGA-SKCM skin cutaneous melanoma cohort. One row per tumor sample with clinical, demographic, and selected molecular features. Illustrative asta-format metadata for the autodiscovery_rl example; the real CSV lives on the reward server side only.

### DATASETS: ###

Dataset Name: tcga_melanoma.csv
Dataset Description: One row per melanoma tumor sample with de-identified clinical and molecular annotations.

### COLUMNS: ###

sample_id:
  De-identified unique identifier for the tumor sample.

age_at_diagnosis:
  Patient age in years at initial pathologic diagnosis.

sex:
  Reported sex of the patient (categorical: female, male).

breslow_depth_mm:
  Breslow tumor thickness in millimeters.

clark_level:
  Clark level of invasion (categorical: I-V).

ulceration:
  Presence of tumor ulceration (categorical: present, absent).

primary_site:
  Anatomic site of the primary tumor (categorical).

braf_mutation:
  BRAF mutation status (categorical: V600E, V600K, wildtype, other).

nras_mutation:
  NRAS mutation status (categorical: mutant, wildtype).

tmb:
  Tumor mutational burden in mutations per megabase.

overall_survival_months:
  Overall survival time in months from diagnosis.

vital_status:
  Vital status at last follow-up (categorical: alive, dead).
